item.title: Interpret a timebank ledger
item.summary: Two organisers discuss whether a timebank ledger captures what members value.
item.transcript_text:
Chair: The timebank ledger shows far fewer exchanges this quarter. Do we conclude that members have stopped helping one another?
Treasurer: Recorded exchanges have fallen, certainly. We recently asked volunteers to record only work that had been agreed in advance, because reimbursements depend on a clear booking. A neighbour who offers ten minutes of help on the spot is no longer counted.
Chair: Then any fall might tell us more about our rule than about demand.
Treasurer: Some of it might. But what is absent from the ledger can still matter for planning. Advance bookings need staffing; informal help may be one reason people stay in the network. I would keep the ledger for reimbursements and ask a short, separate anonymous question about informal exchanges. Neither measure can carry both interpretations by itself.
Chair: So the issue isn't whether the ledger is reliable. It's whether we're asking it to answer the right question.

questions.prompt: What general issue does the discussion illustrate?
options: An incomplete but accurate record can be adequate for one decision and misleading for another
Values that cannot be measured should be excluded from planning
Financial records become less accurate when checked against interviews
Organisations need one comprehensive measure for every use
questions.explanation: The ledger is fit for reimbursement, while a separate source is needed to learn about informal exchange.

questions.prompt: Why is the comparison across quarters limited?
options: The ledger no longer records the same range of activities
Volunteer reimbursements no longer use the ledger
The number of advance bookings was never recorded
Members consciously agreed to help less often
questions.explanation: The inclusion rule changed to cover agreed work, so recorded exchanges need not track the same activity population across quarters.

questions.prompt: What distinction matters to the treasurer?
options: Neighbourhood help and all financial records
The purpose of operational records and the information needed to assess community activity
Advance arrangements and exchanges that require no labour
questions.explanation: Reimbursements and organisational activity ask different questions. Informal assistance can matter even without a ledger entry.

questions.prompt: How should the chair's final comment be understood?
options: It questions the staff member's honesty
It rejects separate informal data collection
It calls for the ledger to cover every claim stakeholders make
It distinguishes accuracy within a purpose from adequacy for another purpose
questions.explanation: A ledger may record its defined transactions accurately yet fail to measure informal help.
